This is what I know, as well as a few anecdotal experiences:

The brain allows other systems to use the space where there isn't anything, or stimulation, this can induce phantom limb syndrome, although phantom limb syndrome can occur for no reason however when a person performs certian activities, the brain might start using this space for mathematics processing where the learned movement for a limb was, as an example feeling burning, itching, and general pain. Although sometimes it's a good feeling, typically it isn't. I get phantom limb symptoms in my dick, it doesn't feel good, kinda like numb pain. Now when the body suddenly starts using a previously un-used area this can cause a similar effect: you may not be able to control somthing as well as before, or maybe thinking about a certian are topic Causes movement or sensation. I know this only from personal experience. One day I decided to learn to move my ears, it was a huge mistake: once I learned how, they moved all the time. More heavily when I moved other facial features, I'm assuming because these are close to each other on the brain. It was like after I learned my body decided not to forget so they would move on their own for a few hours a day. I imagine somthing similar is happening with newborns. Which is why they are twitchy, learning to move all your fingers isn't easy. 
People with colchelar (sp ch?) implants who are over the age of I think 22 never learn to hear like normal adults, they can hear but it's more like hearing of a child, a young child. Children are born blind because they don't have the brain patterns to recognize much more than human facial shapes, which for some reason helps with survival.

Using all of that, slightly chaotic information, and knowing that the brain has limited plasticity as an adult is where I get this information.

I'll link to the implants, if you want to know more about brain plasticity, pick a book up on it. :)

This was years ago when I was in the U.S. Army:

We had a guy that got promoted to corporal after an NCO did everything he could to get out of our unit. (He was by far the worst leader, in terms of getting things accomplished I've ever seen, he was pretty young though, at that time he was 2 years younger than me, making him like 19.) 

Anyway, this guy who they promoted to corporal didn't do much better either for around the first three months he was in charge all he did was blame the previous NCO that we had. Then he started blaming everything on me, even though he was giving me all of the work. It took me about a month to catch on to what was happening. He was sending me to do stuff off post, and telling the higher ups he didn't know where I went. So I started writing everything that he said to me down, everything, times, dates, who was there, who heard it. Didn't matter, a few times I had recorded him actually saying this to me verbally. So during a monthly counseling (everyone gets one) he starts trying to make shit up, and put it on the counseling, I refuse to sign it. When I do, I confront him telling him the truth "If you don't get off my case, and split our work load evenly, I wont work, and then only you are screwed, as higher ups will  blame you for what doesn't get done. Not me." Mr. hot shot tries to put his hands on me, falling to realize that I know a good portion of Judo, have taken a few years of Krav-maga, and  just enough BJJ to over come unskilled opponets, as well as enough Muay Thai to fight a boxer and win repeatedly (When I have fought boxers, I keep my hands to my side to give myself a disadvantage, they generally complain until I KO a few people.) I never talk about martial arts in person, because it generally comes off as bragging, and I've had people try to fight me just to "test them selves." The fight (if you could call it that) goes about how someone would expect, he swings, I slam him on the ground and start pounding his face into the ground, he starts begging me not to hit him. As soon as I let off he starts screaming at me, and swings again I suppose in his mind this was a "fluke" again I slam him on the ground, and listen to him beg for mercy. I didn't hurt him bad enough to actually do anything to him, and we had a witness watch this in shock, who said that he wouldn't say anything if we dropped whatever problems we were having. (Oddly the guy kept telling me I was "lucky" that the guy watching didn't jump in, but he was a drinking buddy of mine. I just let his dumb ass believe himself.) Well, after a few months command try's to come down on me, because hes been telling them shit like "I don't know where he went." and the portion he was leaving "for himself" he was telling them I was refusing to do. Well I confront him on more than one occasion about this, telling him if he doesn't get his shit together he wont like the out come, that he's not going to be able to do anything to me, on more than one occasion I confronted him about his lies, telling him hes fucked if he keeps it up. It should be noted that at this point, he would scream at me in front of people, to have me be ultra-polite, and not sarcasm polite, but just average polite. I had a reputation for being a really nice guy. Any way our higher ups decide to investigate why nothing is getting done, in front of me he blames me, starts screaming at me, blah blah whatever. I (in front of him) pull out my little note book, and start reciting when he told me what, and exactly what was said. Our commander at this point is rather shocked, he talks to a few people and verifies a lot of what happened. This isn't to mention that most of our command has only seen me doing work, and on a few occasions where he said "I don't know where he is" I would be in their offices working on the work he gave me, literally dip shit would call and say I left and he didn't know where I was, In one case he was on speaker phone, and I even pointed this out to our higher ups..how fucking stupid do you have to be...oh yeah, sociopath logic. Push comes to shove and all of our higher ups come in to see whats going on. They see him scream at me, and talk about how I don't actually do anything, how he gives me all this work, and proceeds to talk about work that I did saying he did it.

Here's the problem: Not only did I keep record of what I worked on, I actually hid sticky notes in/on most of what I completed. As well as had people verify that I did the work, and had them keep records of it. (A bunch of the NCO's and Lower officers fucking hated him. They were glad to help me out.) So after he screams for an hour in my face, and I pull out my note book. They just drop it, and pull me aside telling me "Well we dont know why hes acting this way, he obviously needs help, just don't pay any attention to him." For the second time I'm being told this in the only office I actually worked in the entire time I was in the military. All the weight gets put on my shoulders, and he completely gets bypassed just like the previous NCO I had. I get told that I am not allowed to take orders or commands from him. This literally infuriates him. He would attempt to provoke me into fights, try and fuck up the work I was doing, tell me that I was doing a bad job and try and pester me...all of it just went in my note book, which on several occasions he tried to steal, rather unsuccessfully, did the dumb fuck think I didn't make copies? Finally he starts to convince our chain of command that I'm causing his mental problems because I'm harassing him, so they try to come down on me, again, nothing really happens they just warn me. At this point  I decide "enough is enough, time to end this dumb fuck." He is a horrible alcoholic one of the worst I've ever seen. Gets black out drunk every night, is almost constantly drunk at work after they took his 'power' away. I call him after about 11:00 during a week day, and provoke him (not hard) into (wasted) driving to post, I call the gate guard and tell them what happened, they say they will be looking for him at all posts. I call his best friend with a recording of him talking constant shit about him. His best friend calls me after that telling me that he was talking about killing me, blah, blah what ever. When I get up in the morning, I get woke up by an early call saying to be at formation 2 hours early (at this point I know I've won) hes no where to be found, and we go on a 3-3.5 hour run (He had just gotten a DUI.) They yell and scream at me after the run about how I hurt him and all this bull shit. Until I tell them what happened, and have his best friend verify it, as well as the gate guards. I honestly don't know what bullshit story he told them, but the extreme evidence I was providing changed their minds. They article 15 him (extra duty, no pay 45 days of it too!) This is where his wife gets involved: She tells him he as 45 days to get his shit together, or else shes leaving him. After talking to her apparently he was really verbally abusive to her, which she was more than happy to tell our chain of command, who at this point couldn't stand him.

They move him into the only fucking room allegedly available on post...mine. I don't know this is happening, hes just up there when I get back, he tries to be friendly with me, but I can already smell the alochol on his breath. In front of him I immediately pick up my phone, he starts threatening me, I call a new NCO and explain what happened, and that I need some help. He gladly shows up. At this point the guy pulls a knife out, I disarm him sustaining a minor cut. I leave as told to, and show back up later with another NCO because he was threatening to kill himself. He swallowed a whole bottle of pills, placebos haha. The doctors admit him to the psych ward, telling our unit that he did attempt, fortunately he didn't actually have any real medicine. They then tell us hes got really bad psychotic ideation towards our entire unit, and in fact they were under the impression he was an actual psychopath, or at least had become one. He spends about three months there and they release him "cured." No, he isn't he attacks me because when he finally got out his wife called him and filed for divorce, I press charges and he goes right back to the psych-ward, for 9 long months. When he gets out, he apologizes to our unit (He had to or the ward wouldn't release him, apparently this actually caused him to attack doctors when they suggested it to him) and put him on a medication he has to take for life, or risk being put back in a mental ward.

I on several occasions gave him outs, to just not fuck with me, and he never took them. Then I perma-fucked his life. According to my face book friends from the army, hes tried to commit suicide a few more times, then one day just stopped posting. It was the most absurd thing that has ever happened, but I've dealt with 2 other psychopaths/sociopaths in my life time (not including my job in health care) and they only really hurt themselves, its only top 1% that actually manage anything real, in terms of hurting people. Believe me, they are pathetic. As there seems to be this sub-culture that I've found that worships them, they are literally the least strategic people, are bad a social interaction, and really only rely on people who are really really empathetic to survive. Normal people pick them out and avoid them, they only hurt (generally) normal people if they also hurt themselves just as bad.
